candidates.name: blackmarbler
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (World Bank DIME) that automates downloading and processing NASA Black Marble (VIIRS-derived) daily/monthly/annual nighttime-lights composites from NASA LAADS DAAC and aggregating radiance to any user-defined WGS84 polygon. No committed raw data (requires free NASA bearer token); demonstrated with 2012-2022+ near-real-time data (daily lag ~1 week). Actively maintained World Bank org repo.
candidates.why_useful: One-command, point-in-time-capable pull of nightlights for any Airbnb market polygon (city/region) as a tourism/economic-activity proxy at monthly or even daily granularity, addressing gap #5 (engagement/activity proxies) and the broader satellite-tourism-activity theme; because it hits NASA's archive directly it could be re-run vintage-by-vintage for point-in-time construction.
candidates.license: not stated in README excerpt (World Bank org, typically MIT/permissive)
candidates.size_hint: no committed data; API client only

candidates.name: balaton-bshi (Balaton Satellite Health Index)
candidates.what_it_holds: Satellite-based algal-bloom + tourism monitoring system for Lake Balaton, Hungary: 14 lakeside settlements, 3km coastal buffers, 2018-2025 with 2026 projection. Explicitly uses NOAA VIIRS nighttime lights (~500m, monthly) as a 'tourism activity proxy' alongside Sentinel-2 NDCI (algal bloom) and MODIS LST. Output is a JSON file (balaton.json) plus GeoJSON zone definitions powering a bilingual dashboard; intermediate Parquet files not version-controlled.
candidates.why_useful: A working, recent (2026) real-world example of exactly this theme's method — VIIRS nightlights as a tourism-activity proxy at settlement level combined with environmental satellite data — directly reusable as a template/validation case for constructing an analogous nightlights-tourism proxy for Airbnb markets, even though the geography (Hungarian lake resort towns) is outside our current 13/123-market panel.

candidates.name: viirs-nightlights-analysis-tool
candidates.what_it_holds: FastAPI + Leaflet/D3 web tool that pulls Suomi NPP VIIRS DNB monthly composite radiance (NOAA EOG, ~750m, 2012-present) for geocoded cities, applies Elvidge et al. (2021) bias correction, and exports raw + bias-corrected radiance time series (Excel/CSV/JSON) with quality flags. Ships with example city lists: 45 Indian cities, 25 US metros, 30 European capitals, 20 Pakistani cities, plus conflict-zone cities.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made, citable-methodology (bias-corrected) nightlights time-series puller for named cities including several ABNB-relevant US/European metros; could be re-pointed at our 13/123-city Inside Airbnb panel to build a per-market activity index as an occupancy/demand cross-check.
candidates.geography: global (examples: India, US, Europe, Pakistan, conflict zones)
candidates.size_hint: 17 commits; no large committed dataset, generates outputs on run

candidates.name: nighttime-lights (DMSP deblurring)
candidates.what_it_holds: MATLAB academic replication package implementing 'Deblurring DMSP nighttime lights: A new method using Gaussian filters and Frequencies of illumination' (Abrahams et al.) — deblur_roving_window_call_script.m + block_deblur.m. No committed imagery; operates on NOAA NGDC EOG global annual DMSP composites + frequency-of-illumination rasters supplied by the user. 16 commits, 8 stars, 5 forks, MIT-licensed (citation required).
candidates.why_useful: Methods package for sharpening older, low-resolution DMSP nightlights (pre-VIIRS, i.e. pre-2012) — relevant if the team ever wants a longer/older nightlights-based tourism-activity series than VIIRS alone provides, or to make historical nightlights comparable across the DMSP/VIIRS transition.

candidates.name: viirs-nightlights-download
candidates.what_it_holds: Small MIT-licensed downloader script/tool for pulling VIIRS nighttime-light composites directly from NOAA EOG (no committed data). Sibling repo 'geoskill-viirs-nightlights-download' by the same author is essentially the same tool packaged as a 'skill'.
candidates.why_useful: Lightweight alternative acquisition method for VIIRS composites if blackmarbler's NASA-token workflow is inconvenient; low differentiation and unclear activity/maintenance quality versus blackmarbler.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: worldbank/blackmarbler (same underlying data, less mature tool)

candidates.name: COWC - Cars Overhead With Context
candidates.what_it_holds: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory dataset: ~32,000 labeled car bounding boxes across 0.15m-resolution aerial imagery from 6 cities (hosted at gdo152.llnl.gov/cowc/, released 2016). Widely referenced in computer-vision repos (object-detection benchmarks) as the standard overhead car-counting dataset; a GitHub-native mirror/loader was not confirmed but many detector repos (e.g. YOLO/Faster-RCNN car-counting projects) reference it as a data dependency.
candidates.why_useful: Generic reference dataset for training/validating a parking-lot / car-counting-from-overhead-imagery pipeline, which is the closest open, labeled analogue to a satellite-based hotel/retail parking-lot occupancy proxy the team could build for any of its 13/123 Airbnb markets. Not tourism-specific and not on GitHub directly, so only a foundational/methods asset, not an ABNB-ready dataset.
candidates.geography: 6 US/foreign cities (per original paper: Toronto, Selwyn NZ, Potsdam, Vaihingen, Columbus OH, Utah)

candidates.name: SustainBench
candidates.what_it_holds: Stanford Sustain Lab benchmark suite: 15 ML tasks across 7 UN SDGs (poverty/economic development prediction from satellite imagery, cropland/crop-type/yield mapping, health, water/sanitation, brick-kiln land-cover classification). Raw and processed data hosted on Google Drive (external, CC-BY-SA 4.0), with PyTorch dataloaders and preprocessing code in-repo; nightlights use for the poverty-prediction task is implied by the literature this benchmark is built on but not explicitly confirmed in the fetched README excerpt.
candidates.why_useful: Its economic-development-from-satellite-imagery task (poverty prediction using daytime + nighttime imagery, a well-known approach in the development-economics literature) is a transferable methodology for building an activity/wealth proxy per market, though it is not tourism-specific and the nightlights component needs independent confirmation before use.

notes: This theme fell almost entirely into the 'WebSearch budget exhausted' bucket: all three planned WebSearch calls were rejected before running (session-wide budget of 200 already used by other scouts). Fallback search engines reachable via WebFetch were mostly useless: html.duckduckgo.com and lite.duckduckgo.com refused the connection outright (ECONNREFUSED) every time; www.bing.com/search returned syntactically valid pages but with content unrelated to the query (Chinese/Spanish pages, dictionary definitions, generic parking-app sites) on every attempt, suggesting Bing is serving a cached/localized/JS-gated shell rather than real SERP HTML to this fetcher; ecosia.org returned HTTP 403; marginalia and yahoo returned unusable/empty pages. The only reliable channel was `gh search repos`, which was rate-limited (403 'API rate limit exceeded') after ~4-5 calls in quick succession and required ~40-50s waits between bursts; multi-word phrase queries without `in:readme` mostly returned zero hits (gh's default search only checks name/description/topics, not full README), while adding `in:readme` surfaced the two best finds (balaton-bshi, alexeiabrahams/nighttime-lights) before hitting the rate limit again. Net result: this theme is genuinely thin on GitHub — nightlights-as-tourism-proxy is an active academic technique but almost nobody has published a GitHub repo that is BOTH about nightlights AND explicitly tourism-labeled; most hits are generic VIIRS-download tooling (blackmarbler is the strongest, well-maintained, actively used by World Bank) or single-purpose academic side projects (Balaton algal-bloom monitor, DMSP deblurring). Satellite parking-lot-counting specifically returned zero GitHub-native hits in every search method tried (gh search repos on 'parking lot detection satellite', 'parking lot dataset aerial', 'hotel parking lot dataset', 'PKLot parking dataset' all returned empty); the only real dataset found (COWC) is hosted off-GitHub at LLNL and is a generic CV benchmark, not tourism-labeled. Recommend a future pass specifically try `gh search repos` with `in:readme` from a cold rate-limit budget (not chained with other scouts' calls) using terms like 'Orbital Insight', 'SpaceKnow', 'RS Metrics', 'parking lot foot traffic satellite' (these are commercial alt-data vendors whose methodology papers sometimes have open replication code), and Sentinel-2-specific queries like 'beach crowding Sentinel-2' or 'coastal tourism Sentinel index' which were not reached before the rate limit and search-engine failures curtailed this run.
